edits.find: The alias map in `validate-v5.ts` stops being free data and becomes a typed mapping. That is the cost of the prefix being in the type, and it is the only place it is paid.
edits.replace:
The alias map in `validate-v5.ts` stops being free data and becomes a typed mapping. That is the cost of the prefix being in the type, and it is the only place it is paid.

Ownership of `ids` is enforced where the rule id is known and asserted where it is not, and that boundary is worth stating rather than implying. A diagnostic built from a literal rule id, or from one already narrowed to a group as `publishFailureRule` narrows its answer, is checked against its variant by the compiler. The five producers that accept an open `RuleId` cannot be: TypeScript does not narrow a union by a discriminant it knows only the type of, so each passes through one assertion in `contract/diagnostics.ts`, backed by the measurement in `contract/diagnostic-ids.ts` rather than by a proof. Closing that needs those producers to take their `ids` as a rest tuple derived from the rule id they were handed, so a call naming a rule that owns no ids cannot pass one and a call naming a rule that always names ids cannot omit them. That is a slice of its own, because it rewrites every call site of five constructors, and the scope of this record is the union and the discrimination.
